title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 16. Beholding Sri Jagannatha
html:
The Lord delivers seven Gandharvas embodied as tamala trees, dances before Rameshvara at Setubandha, on the way back meets Ramananda Raya again, and returns to Puri and Jagannatha

Verse 1

एवं व्रजन्विप्र पथि प्रवीणां-
स्तमालवृक्षाञ्जगदेकबन्धुः।
दृष्ट्वा हसन्धारणमेव कृत्वा
संस्पर्शनेनापि समुद्दधार॥१॥

evaṁ vrajanvipra pathi pravīṇāṁ-
stamālavṛkṣāñjagadekabandhuḥ|
dṛṣṭvā hasandhāraṇameva kṛtvā
saṁsparśanenāpi samuddadhāra||1||

evam — thus; vrajan — going; vipra — O brahmana; pathi — on the road; pravinan — excellent; tamala-vrikshan — tamala trees; jagat-eka-bandhuh — the one Friend of the world; drishtva — seeing; hasan — laughing; dharanam — embracing; eva — just; kritva — doing; samsparshanena — by the touch; api — even; samuddadhara — delivered.

1Going on His way like this, O brahmana1, the one Friend of the world saw some fine tamala trees; laughing, He embraced them — and by His mere touch He delivered them.

Verse 2

तदैव ते सप्त गन्धर्वरूपा-
स्तद्दर्शनानन्दसमुद्रमग्नाः।
हित्वा स्वपापं मुनिशापजं प्रभुं
नत्वा ययुस्ते निजशासनं शुभम्॥२॥

tadaiva te sapta gandharvarūpā-
staddarśanānandasamudramagnāḥ|
hitvā svapāpaṁ muniśāpajaṁ prabhuṁ
natvā yayuste nijaśāsanaṁ śubham||2||

tada eva — at once; te — they; sapta — seven; gandharva-rupah — in the form of Gandharvas; tat-darshana-ananda-samudra-magnah — sunk in an ocean of bliss at the sight of Him; hitva — casting off; sva-papam — their sin; muni-shapa-jam — born of a sage's curse; prabhum — to the Lord; natva — bowing; yayuh — went; te — they; nija-shasanam — to their own domain; shubham — auspicious.

2At that very moment they took the forms of seven Gandharvas2; sunk in an ocean of bliss at the sight of Him, they cast off the sin born of a sage's curse, bowed to the Lord and departed for their own auspicious realm.

Verse 3

ततः परं कृष्णरसाभिमत्तः
साक्षात्परं ब्रह्म जपञ्छुभाक्षरम्।
श्रीराम गोविन्द हरे मुरारे
जनार्दन श्रीधर वासुदेव॥३॥

tataḥ paraṁ kṛṣṇarasābhimattaḥ
sākṣātparaṁ brahma japañchubhākṣaram|
śrīrāma govinda hare murāre
janārdana śrīdhara vāsudeva||3||

tatah param — after that; krishna-rasa-abhimattah — intoxicated with the rasa of Krishna; sakshat — manifest; param brahma — the Supreme Brahman; japan — repeating; shubha-aksharam — the auspicious syllables; shri-rama — O Sri Rama; govinda — O Govinda; hare — O Hari; murare — O Murari; janardana — O Janardana; shridhara — O Shridhara; vasudeva — O Vasudeva.

3Then the Supreme Brahman made manifest, intoxicated with the rasa of Krishna, went on repeating the auspicious syllables: "Sri Rama! Govinda! Hari! Murari! Janardana! Shridhara! Vasudeva!

Verse 4

स्वभक्तरक्षाकर राघवेन्द्र
सीतापते लक्ष्मणप्राणनाथ।
सुग्रीवहृद्वालिवधातिदुःखित
मरुत्सुतानन्दद रावणारे॥४॥

svabhaktarakṣākara rāghavendra
sītāpate lakṣmaṇaprāṇanātha|
sugrīvahṛdvālivadhātiduḥkhita
marutsutānandada rāvaṇāre||4||

sva-bhakta-raksha-kara — O Protector of Your devotees; raghava-indra — O King of the Raghus; sita-pate — O Lord of Sita; lakshmana-prana-natha — O Lord of Lakshmana's life; sugriva-hrit — O Heart's friend of Sugriva; vali-vadha-ati-duhkhita — O You who grieved deeply over the slaying of Vali; marut-suta-ananda-da — O Giver of joy to the Wind's son; ravana-are — O Enemy of Ravana.

4Protector of Your devotees! King of the Raghus! Lord of Sita! Lord of Lakshmana's life! Heart's friend of Sugriva, who grieved deeply over the slaying of Vali3! Giver of joy to the Wind's son! Enemy of Ravana!"

Verse 5

इत्यादिनामामृतपानमत्तः
श्रीसेतुबन्धं परिव्रज्य सत्वरम्।
ददर्श रामेश्वरलिङ्गमद्भुतं
श्रीशङ्करप्रेष्ठतमः सदा हरिः॥५॥

ityādināmāmṛtapānamattaḥ
śrīsetubandhaṁ parivrajya satvaram|
dadarśa rāmeśvaraliṅgamadbhutaṁ
śrīśaṅkarapreṣṭhatamaḥ sadā hariḥ||5||

iti-adi-nama-amrita-pana-mattah — intoxicated with drinking the nectar of these and other names; shri-setubandham — to Sri Setubandha; parivrajya — wandering; satvaram — quickly; dadarsha — beheld; ramesvara-lingam — the Rameshvara linga; adbhutam — wondrous; shri-shankara-preshthatamah — the dearest to Sri Shankara; sada — ever; harih — Hari.

5Intoxicated with the nectar of these and other names, Hari swiftly reached Sri Setubandha and beheld the wondrous Rameshvara linga4 — for Hari is ever the dearest of all to Sri Shankara.

Verse 6

नत्वा प्रभुमञ्जलिमेव बद्ध्वा
दृष्ट्वा च गौरीरसदं सदाशिवम्।
ननर्त सर्वेश्वर एव तत्र
भावेन गां संनमयन्पदे पदे॥६॥

natvā prabhumañjalimeva baddhvā
dṛṣṭvā ca gaurīrasadaṁ sadāśivam|
nanarta sarveśvara eva tatra
bhāvena gāṁ saṁnamayanpade pade||6||

natva — bowing; prabhum — to the lord (Shiva); anjalim — palms; eva — indeed; baddhva — joining; drishtva — seeing; cha — and; gauri-rasa-dam — the giver of rasa to Gauri; sadashivam — Sadashiva; nanarta — danced; sarva-ishvarah — the Lord of all; eva — Himself; tatra — there; bhavena — in ecstasy; gam — the earth; samnamayan — making bow down; pade pade — at every step.

6Bowing to that lord with joined palms and beholding Sadashiva, the giver of rasa to Gauri, the Lord of all began to dance there, and in His ecstasy the earth bowed down beneath Him at every step.

Verse 7

पश्यन्ति सर्वे जगदेकबन्धुं
श्रीगौरचन्द्रं स्वरसाभिमत्तम्।
बभूवुरत्यन्तसुविस्मया ध्रुवं
तान्वञ्चयित्वा खलु स तिरोऽभवत्॥७॥

paśyanti sarve jagadekabandhuṁ
śrīgauracandraṁ svarasābhimattam|
babhūvuratyantasuvismayā dhruvaṁ
tānvañcayitvā khalu sa tiro'bhavat||7||

pashyanti — see; sarve — all; jagat-eka-bandhum — the one Friend of the world; shri-gaurachandram — Sri Gaurachandra; sva-rasa-abhimattam — intoxicated with His own rasa; babhuvuh — became; atyanta-su-vismayah — utterly amazed; dhruvam — truly; tan — them; vanchayitva — eluding; khalu — indeed; sah — He; tirah abhavat — vanished.

7All who saw Sri Gaurachandra, the one Friend of the world, intoxicated with His own rasa, were utterly amazed — and, eluding them, He vanished from sight.

Verse 8

सर्वाणि तीर्थानि क्रमेण दृष्ट्वा
पुनः परावृत्य कृपाम्बुधिः प्रभुः।
श्रीमज्जगन्नाथदिदृक्षया भृशं
श्रीक्षेत्रराजं गमयाञ्चकार॥८॥

sarvāṇi tīrthāni krameṇa dṛṣṭvā
punaḥ parāvṛtya kṛpāmbudhiḥ prabhuḥ|
śrīmajjagannāthadidṛkṣayā bhṛśaṁ
śrīkṣetrarājaṁ gamayāñcakāra||8||

sarvani — all; tirthani — holy places; kramena — one after another; drishtva — seeing; punah — again; paravritya — turning back; kripa-ambudhih — the ocean of mercy; prabhuh — the Lord; shrimat-jagannatha-didrikshaya — out of the desire to see Sri Jagannatha; bhrisham — intense; shri-kshetra-rajam — to Sri Kshetra, king of holy places; gamayanchakara — made His way.

8Having seen all the holy places one after another, the Lord, the ocean of mercy, turned back and, seized by a strong desire to see Sri Jagannatha, made His way towards Sri Kshetra, the king of holy places.

Verse 9

गोदावरीतीरमनु स्वयं प्रभु-
रागत्य तत्र स्थित एव सद्गतिः।
श्रीरामरायेण पुनः सुपूजितो
बभौ रसज्ञेन द्विजगृहे सुखी॥९॥

godāvarītīramanu svayaṁ prabhu-
rāgatya tatra sthita eva sadgatiḥ|
śrīrāmarāyeṇa punaḥ supūjito
babhau rasajñena dvijagṛhe sukhī||9||

godavari-tiram anu — along the bank of the Godavari; svayam — Himself; prabhuh — the Lord; agatya — coming; tatra — there; sthitah — stayed; eva — indeed; sat-gatih — the refuge of the good; shri-rama-rayena — by Sri Rama Raya (Ramananda Raya); punah — again; su-pujitah — warmly honoured; babhau — shone; rasa-jnena — the knower of rasa; dvija-grihe — in a brahmana's house; sukhi — happy.

9Following the bank of the Godavari, the Lord, the refuge of the good, came there and stayed; and, warmly honoured once more by Sri Ramananda Raya, the knower of rasa, He shone with happiness in a brahmana's house.

Verse 10

रात्रौ परं तीर्थकथाः प्रजल्प-
ञ्छ्रीराधिकाकृष्णरसानुमोदितः।
आज्ञाप्य शीघ्रं च श्रीपद्मलोचनं
द्रष्टुं सदैवार्हसि नापरं सुखम्॥१०॥

rātrau paraṁ tīrthakathāḥ prajalpa-
ñchrīrādhikākṛṣṇarasānumoditaḥ|
ājñāpya śīghraṁ ca śrīpadmalocanaṁ
draṣṭuṁ sadaivārhasi nāparaṁ sukham||10||

ratrau — at night; param — then; tirtha-kathah — talks about the holy places; prajalpan — conversing; shri-radhika-krishna-rasa-anumoditah — delighting in the rasa of Sri Radhika and Krishna; ajnapya — commanding; shighram — soon; cha — and; shri-padma-lochanam — the holy Lotus-eyed One; drashtum — to see; sada — always; eva — indeed; arhasi — you should; na — no; aparam — other; sukham — happiness.

10At night they talked of the holy places, delighting in the rasa of Sri Radhika and Krishna; and then the Lord commanded: "Come soon — you should always behold the holy Lotus-eyed One: there is no other happiness."

Verse 11

एवं निशा सा रसिकेन्द्रमौलिना
श्रीगौरचन्द्रेण रायेण सार्धम्।
नीता क्षणप्रायमतीव दर्शना-
त्पुनः स्वयं गन्तुमना बभूव ह॥११॥

evaṁ niśā sā rasikendramaulinā
śrīgauracandreṇa rāyeṇa sārdham|
nītā kṣaṇaprāyamatīva darśanā-
tpunaḥ svayaṁ gantumanā babhūva ha||11||

evam — thus; nisha — night; sa — that; rasika-indra-maulina — by the crown of the kings of rasikas; shri-gaurachandrena — by Sri Gaurachandra; rayena — with the Raya; sardham — together; nita — was spent; kshana-prayam — like a moment; ativa — from the intense; darshanat — (joy of) seeing; punah — again; svayam — Himself; gantu-manah — minded to go; babhuva — became; ha — indeed.

11Thus the crown of the kings of rasikas, Sri Gaurachandra, spent that night with the Raya — in the joy of their meeting it passed like a moment; and once more He was minded to set out.

Verse 12

श्रीविष्णुदासेन द्विजेन सार्ध-
मालालनाथं स जनार्दनं प्रभुः।
दृष्ट्वा प्रणम्य निवसन्कियद्दिन-
मायाति सर्वेश्वरनीलकन्दरम्॥१२॥

śrīviṣṇudāsena dvijena sārdha-
mālālanāthaṁ sa janārdanaṁ prabhuḥ|
dṛṣṭvā praṇamya nivasankiyaddina-
māyāti sarveśvaranīlakandaram||12||

shri-vishnudasena — with Sri Vishnudasa; dvijena — a brahmana; sardham — together; alalanatham — Alalanatha; sah — He; janardanam — Janardana; prabhuh — the Lord; drishtva — seeing; pranamya — bowing; nivasan — staying; kiyad-dinam — some days; ayati — comes; sarva-ishvara-nila-kandaram — to the Blue Cave of the Lord of all.

12Together with the brahmana Sri Vishnudasa the Lord beheld Janardana at Alalanatha5, bowed to Him, stayed there some days, and came to the Blue Cave6 of the Lord of all.

Verse 13

श्रीकाशीनाथस्य गृहे स्थितो हरिः
श्रीसार्वभौमादिभिरन्वितः स्वयम्।
श्रीमज्जगन्नाथदिदृक्षया ययौ
प्रक्षाल्य पादौ श्रीरत्नमन्दिरम्॥१३॥

śrīkāśīnāthasya gṛhe sthito hariḥ
śrīsārvabhaumādibhiranvitaḥ svayam|
śrīmajjagannāthadidṛkṣayā yayau
prakṣālya pādau śrīratnamandiram||13||

shri-kashinathasya — of Sri Kashinatha; grihe — in the house; sthitah — staying; harih — Hari; shri-sarvabhauma-adibhih — by Sri Sarvabhauma and others; anvitah — accompanied; svayam — Himself; shrimat-jagannatha-didrikshaya — wishing to see Sri Jagannatha; yayau — went; prakshalya — washing; padau — His feet; shri-ratna-mandiram — to the holy jewel-temple.

13Staying in the house of Sri Kashinatha, Hari, accompanied by Sri Sarvabhauma and others, washed His feet and, longing to see Sri Jagannatha, went to the holy jewel-temple.

Verse 14

श्रीगरुडस्तम्भसमास्थितः श्री-
कृष्णः स्वयं भक्तिरसेन पूर्णः।
ददर्श सर्वेश्वरमीश्वरं परं
ब्रह्म स्वयं साग्रजमेव श्रीपतिः॥१४॥

śrīgaruḍastambhasamāsthitaḥ śrī-
kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṁ bhaktirasena pūrṇaḥ|
dadarśa sarveśvaramīśvaraṁ paraṁ
brahma svayaṁ sāgrajameva śrīpatiḥ||14||

shri-garuda-stambha-samasthitah — standing by the holy pillar of Garuda; shri-krishnah — Sri Krishna; svayam — Himself; bhakti-rasena — with the rasa of devotion; purnah — filled; dadarsha — beheld; sarva-ishvaram — the Lord of all; ishvaram — the Lord; param brahma — the Supreme Brahman; svayam — Himself; sa-agrajam — with His elder brother; eva — indeed; shri-patih — the Husband of Shri.

14Standing by the holy pillar of Garuda7, Sri Krishna Himself, the Husband of Shri, filled with the rasa of devotion, beheld the Lord of all, the Lord, the Supreme Brahman — Himself, together with His elder brother.

Verse 15

पार्श्वद्वये श्यामलगौरसुन्दरौ
पश्यन्ति भक्ताः सुखसिन्धुमग्नाः।
न तृप्तिमापुः कृपणा धनं यथा
संप्राप्य कुत्रापि न वक्तुमीशिरे॥१५॥

pārśvadvaye śyāmalagaurasundarau
paśyanti bhaktāḥ sukhasindhumagnāḥ|
na tṛptimāpuḥ kṛpaṇā dhanaṁ yathā
saṁprāpya kutrāpi na vaktumīśire||15||

parshva-dvaye — side by side; shyamala-gaura-sundarau — the Beautiful Dark One and the Beautiful Golden One; pashyanti — see; bhaktah — the devotees; sukha-sindhu-magnah — sunk in an ocean of happiness; na — not; triptim — satiety; apuh — reached; kripanah — misers; dhanam — wealth; yatha — as; samprapya — having gained; kutra api — anywhere; na — not; vaktum — to speak; ishire — were able.

15And the devotees, sunk in an ocean of happiness, beheld side by side the Beautiful Dark One and the Beautiful Golden One8, and could not have enough of the sight; and like misers who have come upon wealth, they could not speak of it to anyone.

Verse 16

पश्यञ्छ्रीभक्तवर्गैः सकलरसगुरुर्गौरप्रेम्णि निमग्नो
नित्यानन्दाख्यरामो रसमयवपुषौ श्यामगौराङ्गरूपौ।
हुङ्कारैः सिंहनादैर्जयजयध्वनिभिस्ताण्डवैरप्यभीक्ष्णं
सर्वेषां प्रेमदाता जयति स गदाधारिणो दर्शपूर्णः॥१६॥

paśyañchrībhaktavargaiḥ sakalarasagururgaurapremṇi nimagno
nityānandākhyarāmo rasamayavapuṣau śyāmagaurāṅgarūpau|
huṅkāraiḥ siṁhanādairjayajayadhvanibhistāṇḍavairapyabhīkṣṇaṁ
sarveṣāṁ premadātā jayati sa gadādhāriṇo darśapūrṇaḥ||16||

pashyan — seeing; shri-bhakta-vargaih — with the hosts of devotees; sakala-rasa-guruh — the guru of every rasa; gaura-premni — in love for Gaura; nimagnah — immersed; nityananda-akhya-ramah — Rama named Nityananda; rasa-maya-vapushau — the two forms made of rasa; shyama-gaura-anga-rupau — the dark one and the golden one; hunkaraih — with roars; simha-nadaih — with lion-cries; jaya-jaya-dhvanibhih — with shouts of "Jaya! Jaya!"; tandavaih — with wild dances; api — and; abhikshnam — incessantly; sarvesham — to all; prema-data — the giver of love; jayati — glory be to; sah — him; gada-dharinah — of the Bearer of the mace; darsha-purnah — filled with the sight.

16Glory to Him — to Rama named Nityananda, the guru of every rasa, immersed in love for Gaura, the giver of love to all! With the hosts of devotees He gazed on the two forms made of rasa, the dark and the golden, and ceaselessly He roared, gave lion-cries, shouted "Jaya! Jaya!" and danced wildly, filled with the sight of the Bearer of the mace9.

Verse 17

तदैव श्रीकृष्णसमाज्ञया सुधी-
र्माल्यं समादाय तुलसीविमिश्रकम्।
श्रीगौरचन्द्राय स भक्तमानिने
सभक्तवर्गाय ददौ महामतिः॥१७॥

tadaiva śrīkṛṣṇasamājñayā sudhī-
rmālyaṁ samādāya tulasīvimiśrakam|
śrīgauracandrāya sa bhaktamānine
sabhaktavargāya dadau mahāmatiḥ||17||

tada eva — just then; shri-krishna-samajnaya — by the command of Sri Krishna (Jagannatha); sudhih — the wise (priest); malyam — the garland; samadaya — taking; tulasi-vimishrakam — mixed with tulasi; shri-gaurachandraya — to Sri Gaurachandra; sah — he; bhakta-manine — who regarded Himself as a devotee; sa-bhakta-vargaya — together with the host of devotees; dadau — gave; maha-matih — high-minded.

17Just then the wise and high-minded priest, at Sri Krishna's command, took His garland, entwined with tulasi, and offered it to Sri Gaurachandra, who regarded Himself as a mere devotee, and to all His devotees.

Verse 18

प्रसादमालां जगदीश्वरस्य
प्रेमाश्रुपूर्णः किल लोकपावनः।
सभक्तवर्गः पुलकाकुलावृतो
जग्राह मूर्ध्ना प्रणमन्स्वयं हरिः॥१८॥

prasādamālāṁ jagadīśvarasya
premāśrupūrṇaḥ kila lokapāvanaḥ|
sabhaktavargaḥ pulakākulāvṛto
jagrāha mūrdhnā praṇamansvayaṁ hariḥ||18||

prasada-malam — the prasada garland; jagat-ishvarasya — of the Lord of the world; prema-ashru-purnah — full of tears of love; kila — indeed; loka-pavanah — the Purifier of the world; sa-bhakta-vargah — with the host of devotees; pulaka-akula-avritah — covered with thrilling hair; jagraha — took; murdhna — on His head; pranaman — bowing; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari.

18The Purifier of the world, Hari Himself, full of tears of love and thrilling all over, together with His devotees received the prasada garland of the Lord of the world upon His head, bowing low.

Thus ends the sixteenth sarga, "Beholding Sri Jagannatha" (Shri-jagannatha-darshana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Murari is addressing Damodara Pandita, his interlocutor.
  2. Gandharvas: celestial singers and musicians. In the "Chaitanya Charitamrita" (Madhya 9) a similar story is told of seven tala palms touched by the Lord.
  3. The sense of this epithet in the editions is unclear; the translation is conjectural.
  4. Setubandha: the place on the southern coast from which Rama built the bridge to Lanka; Rameshvara: the linga of Shiva said to have been installed by Rama.
  5. Alalanatha: a temple of Vishnu at Brahmagiri, south of Puri (cf. sarga 14).
  6. That is, to Nilachala (the "Blue Mountain"), Puri.
  7. The Garuda pillar in the temple of Jagannatha, from which Sri Chaitanya used to behold the Deity.
  8. The Dark One is Jagannatha; the Golden One is Sri Chaitanya Himself, standing before Him.
  9. The end of the verse is corrupt in the editions; it may also be understood as "filled with the sight of Gadadhara." The translation is conjectural.
